Chapter 9: Trust, Systems, and the Fragility of Security.
Imagine this: years after leaving his old life behind, the former con artist turned into a true expert on trust. He’d seen just how quickly trust can fall apart... and how tough it is to put back together.
He realized something big—our lives are deeply connected to all sorts of systems. Think about banks, hospitals, schools—places we rely on every single day. But here’s the thing... those systems are only as secure as the people running them.
He’d walk through busy offices and spot the same mistakes he once took advantage of. Maybe you’ve seen them too—passwords scribbled on sticky notes, doors left open, or employees ready to help anyone who looks the part. It turns out, most security breaches aren’t caused by some genius hacker. Nope, it’s usually just simple human error.
He liked to share stories—like how a friendly smile and a clipboard could get you almost anywhere, or how someone with a confident voice on the phone could talk their way into getting sensitive info. There’s a lesson in all of this: systems are fragile, mostly because people want to trust. The answer isn’t to get suspicious of everyone... it’s to get more aware.
So, he started working with organizations to help them put better safeguards in place. He taught people how to spot the warning signs of a scam. But deep down, he knew—even the best systems aren’t perfect. The real trick? Creating a culture where it’s normal to ask questions, where saying “no” is totally okay, and where trust has to be earned—not just given away.
Most of us want to believe the world is safe, that the rules will always protect us. But here’s something important to remember... security is everyone’s job. It’s something we build together, day by day, with every choice we make and every question we ask.
